# The Shadow That Stretches Toward Dawn

## Scripture
*"He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end."* — Ecclesiastes 3:11

## Reflection
Step outside on a late October evening and you'll notice the shadows arriving earlier now. The sun sets sooner, the darkness stretches longer, and the crisp air carries the scent of fading leaves. It's the season of diminishing light—and yet the sky offers a quiet gift: the zodiacal light.

This faint, ghostly glow appears along the horizon just after sunset or before sunrise, a subtle cone of light reflecting off dust scattered across our solar system. Most nights, it goes unnoticed. But when the sky is darkest and the air is clearest—often in autumn—it becomes visible, a whisper of brightness where you'd expect only black.

There's something deeply comforting in this phenomenon. Even in the longest nights, light lingers. Even when the sun has vanished from view, its glow still reaches us through particles floating silently between the planets. Creation itself testifies that darkness is never total, that God's handiwork leaves traces even in the shadows.

Solomon observed that God "set eternity in the human heart"—a longing for something beyond the here and now. The zodiacal light is a gentle reminder that our longing is not misplaced. The God who scattered dust across the cosmos and set it to catch the light of a hidden sun is the same God who promises that our seasons of dimness are held within His larger story. Nothing is wasted. Even the dust reflects glory.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for the quiet reminders that light persists even when we cannot see the source. When life feels dim and shadows lengthen, help us trust that Your glory still reaches us. Set our hearts on eternity, and let even the faintest glimmers point us toward You. Amen.
